message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to live air‑quality data, so I can’t tell you the exact AQI for Los Angeles at this moment. However, you can quickly check the current conditions using one of the following reliable sources:

| Service | How to use |
|---------|------------|
| **AirNow** (U.S. EPA) | Visit https://www.airnow.gov/, enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code, and view the latest AQI, pollutant breakdown, and health recommendations. |
| **AQICN** (World Air Quality Index) | Go to https://aqicn.org/, search for “Los Angeles,” and see the real‑time AQI, forecast, and historical data. |
| **Weather apps** (e.g., Weather.com, AccuWeather, or your phone’s native weather app) | Many include an AQI widget for major cities. |
| **Local news websites** | Stations like KABC, KNBC, or local public‑broadcasting sites often post daily air‑quality updates. |

If you’re looking for a quick snapshot, you can also try a voice assistant (Google Assistant, Siri, Alexa) and ask, “What’s the air quality in Los Angeles?” They usually pull from the same data sources.

Let me know if you’d like help interpreting the AQI numbers or understanding what the different pollutant levels mean!
